summary: Lunar Landing Site Navigator is an interactive browser-based tool that lets mission planners, educators, and the public visualize Sun and Earth positions at candidate landing sites near the Moon's south pole. Users select from six real candidate sites (Shackleton, Haworth, Nobile, Malapert, Leibnitz, Connecting Ridge) or enter custom coordinates, then scrub through a full lunar day (708 hours) to see live horizon views showing solar elevation for power generation assessment and Earth elevation for direct-to-Earth communication windows. A 30-day timeline plots both curves with shaded viable windows, and a Site Comparison tab ranks all sites by illumination percentage and Earth visibility enabling rapid, intuitive trade-off analysis without complex interfaces.
details:
Lunar Landing Site Navigator is a self-contained web application built to address the core challenge: making Sun and Earth position data at Moon south-pole landing sites fast and intuitive to evaluate.

How it works:
The tool uses Julian Date-based solar ephemeris (low-precision analytical model), lunar orbital elements, and selenographic elevation math (great-circle formula from sub-solar and sub-Earth points on the lunar surface) to compute real-time azimuth and elevation of the Sun and Earth from any point on the Moon. All calculations run client-side in the browser with no server or external API required.

Features:
- Horizon View: Two side-by-side rendered horizon panels showing Sun (power) and Earth (comms) position with elevation angle, azimuth, capacity bars, and sky visualization
- 30-Day Timeline: Elevation curves for both bodies over a full lunar day with shaded power and comms windows and a live time cursor
- Site Comparison: Automated 30-day statistics for all six candidate sites — solar illumination % and Earth visibility % — rendered as bar charts for instant ranking
- Animation: Sweep through the full 708-hour lunar day at adjustable speed to watch windows open and close
- Custom coordinates: Longitude and latitude sliders to evaluate any south-pole location

Tools and languages used:
HTML5, CSS3, vanilla JavaScript, HTML Canvas API. No external libraries or dependencies.

Impact:
The tool makes mission-critical lighting and communication data accessible to non-specialists — students, public audiences, and early-stage planners — without requiring specialized software or complex interfaces.
